origins.section: A Warm Start Survives Some Changes Better Than Others
Not Every Solver Warm-Starts Through MathOpt
A Dual Value Predicts a Small Change; Re-Solve to Know a Large One

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-changes: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-changes: "**A new row** can cut the old vertex off. The plan was carrying $50,886k in total, ten times the new cap of $5,000k, so a large part of the plan has to change. The warm start still saved something, 116 pivots against 189, but far less than for the other edits."
recorded.prompt:q-solver: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-solver: "GLOP's re-solve took 216 pivots against 4,660 from scratch. HiGHS and PDLP did exactly the work of a cold solve: through MathOpt in OR-Tools 9.15, their incremental re-solves start over."
recorded.prompt:q-dual: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-dual: "So for a cut, $`z - y \cdot \text{cut}`$ is an **upper bound** on the new optimum: the real loss can only be larger." ... "'a cut of $11.5M costs at least $5.5M of NPV'; the re-solve then says it costs $5.96M." (10,000 − 0.8 × 3,000 = 7,600)

recorded.prompt:q-changes:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-changes:c: "**A new variable** leaves the old vertex allowed too, with the new share at 0. Four pivots fit the new project in."
recorded.prompt:q-changes:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-changes:d: "edits that move a bound or a coefficient by a little are cheap to re-solve warm". Reference table: "row limit, small change | same basis, maybe broken rows | 0 to 6 pivots".
recorded.prompt:q-solver:a: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-solver:a: "HiGHS and PDLP did exactly the work of a cold solve: through MathOpt in OR-Tools 9.15, their incremental re-solves start over."
recorded.prompt:q-solver:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-solver:b: Same passage. Also "PDLP iterations: base 320 after the cut, warm 384 cold 384".
recorded.prompt:q-solver:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-solver:c: "`IncrementalSolver` accepts every solver; whether the next solve starts from the last one is up to the solver."
recorded.prompt:q-dual:b: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dual:b: "From $1,000k on, the basis changes ... and the prediction drifts further from the truth with every size of cut." The prediction is only an upper bound.
recorded.prompt:q-dual:c: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dual:c: "for a cut, $`z - y \cdot \text{cut}`$ is an **upper bound** on the new optimum: the real loss can only be larger." Also "every later $k cut costs at least as much as the one before", the opposite of the option's reason.
recorded.prompt:q-dual:d: Using only what the lesson page states, does a passage of the page rule this option out? Cite the passage, or say none does or that the option is partly true. Be strict.
recorded.outcome:q-dual:d: The rate is the dual value: "The **dual value** of a row ... is the rate at which the optimal objective changes as the row's limit changes". That is 0.8 here, not 1, and the exact value needs a re-solve (heading: "Re-Solve to Know a Large One"). Note: 7,000 itself is under the 7,600 bound, so the page rules out the reason and the certainty, not the number.
